something has. Content `input` and `change` events mark it changed, and
actions marked `data-needs-changes`, such as Save, stay disabled until
then. The question replaces the content in the same surface rather than
opening a second layer.

declarations.description:
A site or app header pinned to the top of the page, with a brand, nav
links and actions, full width with its content kept to the content width.
It's transparent at first, then gets a blurred surface and a bottom border
once the page scrolls, or once the element
`reveal-after` names scrolls out of view, such as a hero. With
`reveal-after` the brand stays hidden, taking no room, until then, so a
large logo in the hero hands over to the small one in the bar. The nav
slides over as it opens.

`overlay` lays it over the top of the page rather than taking room, for a
page that opens with a hero. Below `menu-below`, 600px wide by default,
the nav moves into a menu opened from a button, which closes on Esc, a
click outside or a link. Raise it when the nav and actions need more room.
With no nav links there's no menu button, so a bar of only a brand and
actions keeps its layout at every width.

declarations.description:
A native button styled through `--gw-*` variables, so it follows the
theme and mode around it. With `href` it renders a link that looks the
same. Put an icon in the `icon` slot.

For a link the page's HTML has to carry, such as one with `rel="me"`, a
`target` or `aria-current="page"`, put a plain `<a>` inside instead of
`href`. The button styles it, a click anywhere on the pill follows it, and
`aria-current` on it gets a current style.

`variant` picks the color and `appearance` how it's applied, from most to
least important: `accent` (a solid fill), `filled` (a soft tint),
`outlined` (a stroke) or `plain` (text only). Every button is a pill.
Sizes run `xs` to `xl`, and `--gw-button-scale` sets any size in between.

While `loading`, a spinning ring takes the icon's place, or the text's
when there's no icon, so the button keeps its size, and clicks are
ignored. The icon fades back once it's done.

A surface for one group of content, with an optional heading and actions.
With `href` the whole card is a link. While `loading`, lines of skeleton
stand in for the content, and for the heading until it's known. The card
glides to its new height and the content fades in once it's loaded.

For a link the page's HTML has to carry, such as one with a `target` or
`rel`, put an `<a>` in the `heading` slot instead of `href`. A click
anywhere on the card that isn't on another control follows it, the card
shows the link's hover and focus, and the link stays a real one in the
page, so the rest of the card's content stays plain text.

declarations.description:
A button that opens a menu on the Popover API, so it shows in the top
layer and closes on Esc or a click outside. Set `items`; arrow keys, Home
and End move between them, and choosing one fires `select` with its
`value` and closes the menu.

Contextual actions, such as "Add a schedule", go in `actions`: they stay
below the items as the list scrolls, so they're found without scrolling to
the end, and with no items the menu says `empty` above them.

For a menu of choices, such as sort and order, give each item `checked`:
the picked one shows a tick, and `separator` starts the next group.
Items with `checkbox` toggle instead, firing `check` and keeping the menu
open, and `group` lists items under a heading.

Items render inside the component, so a page's own button styles can't
reach them.

A labeled select whose list opens under it, after Home Assistant's
pickers. Long lists get a search field, focused as the list opens, and
only the options in view are rendered. Move with the arrow keys and pick
with Enter. Below 600px wide the list is a bottom sheet.

Pass `options`, or write `<option>` children (in `<optgroup>`s for
groups, with `data-icon`, `data-swatch` and `data-description`), which it
reads once when it first connects. A hidden input carries the value in
forms, and it fires `change` when the value changes.

With `multiple` it picks several: each pick toggles an option in `values`
and the list stays open, the trigger shows the first choice and how many
more, and a Clear button under the list empties it. A hidden input per
value carries them in forms.

declarations.description:
The page's mode, theme and import, in place where there's room and in a
popover where there isn't. Offers the mode (auto, light, dark or Darker),
the theme, and buttons to import a theme file (a Groundwork theme's `.json`
or an Omarchy `colors.toml`) or reset.

It only asks: it fires `mode`, `theme`, `import` and `reset`, and the page
applies them and sets `mode`, `theme` and `themes` back. `pageTheme` from
`@timmo001/groundwork-tokens/page` does all of that. Show an import's
result, such as contrast misses, in `status`.

`gallery` swaps the theme select for `gw-theme-gallery`'s cards, which
preview each theme in the chosen mode.

`layout` sets how it shows. `auto`, the default, lays the mode out as icons
and the theme as a select in place while they fit the room it's given,
then moves them into the popover, the theme first, as the room runs out.
Reset, Import, the gallery and `status` stay in the popover, opened from a
palette button. Once the mode and theme are in place and only Reset and
Import are left, they're a ⋮ menu instead.
In a flex row, such as `gw-page-header`'s actions, it gives up room before
the title does. `popover` keeps everything behind the palette button. `cycle` is one button
showing the mode in use, which steps to the next mode on each press, for an
app bar. `inline` lays every control out in place, in one wrapping row with
Reset and Import, for a footer or a settings page; set `justify-content` on
it to align the row. With `gallery`, the cards take a row of their own
under it. `modes` picks which modes it offers, such as
`light dark` without Auto.

declarations.name: motionDuration
declarations.description:
Reads a motion duration token in milliseconds, such as
`--gw-motion-slow`, falling back when the tokens aren't loaded.

declarations.name: fadeEasing
declarations.description:
The curve for fades. A decelerating curve lands most of an opacity change
in the first frames and reads as a pop, so fades ease in and out.

declarations.name: fadeIn
declarations.description:
Fades `element` in, after `delay`, over `duration` (`--gw-motion-slow` by
default). Use it when content replaces a skeleton. With reduced motion it
shows at once.

declarations.name: animateHeight
declarations.description:
Glides `element` from the height it had before a change to the height it
has after, as an expansion panel opens, so content arriving or going never
jumps the layout. Measure with `before = element.offsetHeight` ahead of the
change, then call this once it's rendered. Skipped when motion is reduced.

declarations.name: withViewTransition
declarations.description:
Runs a DOM change inside a View Transition where the browser supports one
and motion isn't reduced, otherwise runs it straight away, after Home
Assistant's `withViewTransition()`. Use it for changes to the whole view,
such as switching theme or mode; component state uses CSS transitions.

The change may return a promise, such as a Lit element's
`updateComplete`, so the new view is captured once it has rendered. Keep
it quick: the page is frozen until it settles.

declarations.name: on
declarations.description:
Adds a listener for one of the element's own events, typed from its
`@fires` docs, and returns a function that removes it.

declarations.name: scrollbars
declarations.description:
The page's scrollbars for a shadow root: a small rounded thumb on a clear
track with no arrow buttons, squaring off at the ends of its track. Every
`gw-` element adopts it; add it to an app's own components' styles to match.
The `--gw-scrollbar-*` properties restyle it as they do the page's.

declarations.name: followPageScroll
declarations.description:
Sets `--gw-scrollbar-top`, `-bottom`, `-left` and `-right` on the root as
the page scrolls, 0 against that end and 1 elsewhere, so the window's
scrollbar thumb squares off at the ends like the others. The window's
scrollbar doesn't repaint for the scroll-driven animation the themes give
other scrollers. Every `gw-` element starts it when it's defined.

declarations.name: controlSizes
declarations.description:
The `xs` to `xl` presets on a `size` attribute, as `--gw-<name>-scale`
around 1 for medium, so an app can also set any size between or beyond
them. A control multiplies its height and icon by `--gw-control-scale`
too, which follows the theme's density, and its text only by its own
scale, since spacing and type already follow density on their own.
